lessons.title: Slow sunrise
body: Attack is how fast a note reaches full loudness after you press a key. Instant attack: a switch. Slow attack: a sunrise.
Strings and pads swell in. Drums and plucks hit immediately. This knob alone changes the instrument's personality.

goal.hint: Make each note swell in like a sunrise - no click, no instant hit.

lessons.title: Short and snappy
body: After the attack, the sound falls to its sustain level. Decay sets how fast it falls; sustain sets where it lands.
Here the sustain is parked at silence, so decay alone decides how long the note lives. Short decay: a pluck. Long decay: a bell.

goal.hint: Make it snappy - a plucked string, not a bell.

lessons.title: Let it ring
body: Release is what happens after your finger leaves the key. Zero release: the sound snaps shut. Long release: it floats away.
Release is why some sounds feel airy and others feel chopped. Match the target's tail - listen to how long it rings after the note ends.

goal.hint: Let it float away - a long, gentle tail after each note.
